articles.title: Instacart scraps AI pricing tests that made some products more expensive
articles.summary: Instacart says it will no longer allow retailers to run pricing experiments, which resulted in some customers seeing higher prices on the same products than others.
articles.body: Instacart is ending its AI-powered pricing tests, which led some users to see higher prices on certain products than others. “Now, if two families are shopping for the same items, at the same time, from the same store location on Instacart, they see the same prices — period,” Instacart writes in a blog post on Monday. The change comes just weeks after a study from Groundwork Collaborative, Consumer Reports, and More Perfect Union found that Instacart offered multiple price points for the same grocery items at the same store. The report drew attention from lawmakers, including Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY), who said in a letter to the Federal Trade Commission that “consumers deserve to know when they are being placed into pricing tests.” Reuters also reported that the FTC opened an investigation into Instacart’s AI pricing tests. Instacart says it will no longer allow retailers to use the AI-powered Eversight technology it acquired in 2022 to run pricing tests, though retailers “may choose to vary the price of items on a store-by-store basis.” It adds that the pricing tests “were never based on supply or demand, personal data, demographics, or individual shopping behavior.” Last week, Instacart reached a $60 million settlement with the agency over separate allegations that it engaged in deceptive tactics, including falsely advertising free shipping. “We’ve listened carefully to feedback from our customers. And we understand that the tests we ran with a small number of retail partners that resulted in different prices for the same item at the same store missed the mark for some customers,” Instacart says.

articles.title: Oura pulls $15bn stock market listing days after announcement
articles.summary: The wearable technology company had been expected to list its shares in the US.
articles.body:
Oura has pulled its plan to sell shares in its business on the US stock market, in a move which would have valued the firm at $15bn (£11.3bn), just days after announcing it.

The maker of smart rings which track their owners' health said it would postpone its flotation "due to uncertainty in the Initial Public Offering (IPO) market" and did not say when it might go ahead.

Oura had filed official documents setting out plans to raise up to $2.2bn by offering shares in the business to investors just over a week ago.

The tech firm has become the latest business to delay its public listing, with experts saying the IPO market is getting more challenging.

Oura's chief executive Tom Hale said "an IPO is just one step in our journey", adding that "we have the luxury of choosing our moment".

Earlier this month, US nuclear technology firm Holtec International also postponed its flotation. It blamed an "unusual confluence of developments that has impaired investor confidence in the market for new public offerings".

In particular, it cited rising energy costs, military conflicts, global trade tensions and concerns about inflation which have led to central banks including the US Federal Reserve raising benchmark interest rates.

This week, the yield – or interest rate – on US debt repayable in 10 years' time hit the highest level since 2007.

Samuel Kerr, global head of equity capital markets at Mergermarket, said: "What is now clear is we are in a very different IPO market to the one we envisaged just a few weeks ago."

Oura had planned to sell shares priced at between $40 and $44 on the Nasdaq stock market index, giving the company an implied market value of $15bn.

In its last full financial year, ending 30 September 2025, Oura made a pre-tax profit of $23.5m on sales $907.8m. That compares to a $6.2m pre-tax profit in the previous year.

Its most recent figures for the nine months to 30 June this year show pre-tax income of $70m on sales of $1.2bn.

Oura, founded in Finland in 2013, has its global headquarters in San Francisco and makes smart rings – costing upwards of $300 – which monitor things such as its owner's heartbeat and sleep patterns which are analysed and presented on an app.

The company is the subject of a class action lawsuit which accused it of false advertising by claiming its rings can accurately track a person's sleep activity and patterns.

The lawsuit, filed by the Clarkson Law Firm in August, claimed: "Oura rings cannot measure one's sleep or cycles. That's because sleep happens in the brain, not on one's finger."

It is understood that Oura's decision to delay an IPO is not connected to the lawsuit.

In a statement, a spokesperson for Oura said: "We stand behind our science, research and accuracy claims."

They added: "Like other consumer sleep wearables, Oura Ring estimates sleep stages using multiple physiological signals, including heart rate, heart rate variability, movement, breathing patterns, and temperature."

articles.title: More Ways to Disrupt: New 2026 Side Events from KOTRA, WayFounder, Enterprise Ireland, SafetyWing + Descope | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Disrupt doesn’t end when you leave Moscone West. 👀 Founder dinners, investor meetups, happy hours, workshops, roundtables and more are taking over San Francisco during Disrupt Week. See what’s happening, find your people, and start building your calendar.
articles.body:
TechCrunch Disrupt is where the tech community comes together to build, debate, and connect. And during Disrupt Week, that conversation doesn’t stop when the doors to Moscone West close.

Our Side Events program brings founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders together across San Francisco for everything from intimate roundtables and founder gatherings to happy hours, dinners, workshops, and community meetups.

Whether you’re looking to make a few new connections, find your next collaborator, go deep on a specific industry, or just get out of conference mode for a minute, there’s a lot happening beyond the show floor.

Explore the 2026 Side Events, and find your people.

Meet 18 emerging startups from the Republic of Korea for an evening of founder conversations, curated introductions, and networking with investors, operators, corporate leaders, and fellow entrepreneurs. Each founder will give a quick introduction before the evening opens up for conversations and connections across the U.S. and global startup ecosystem. Hosted by: WayFounder RSVP

Head to Harrington’s Irish Pub for an evening of drinks and conversation with founders, HR leaders, and members of the startup community. Hosted by SafetyWing during TechCrunch Disrupt, the happy hour offers a casual setting to meet new people and connect with the team behind the startup’s approach to health coverage for remote and global teams. Hosted by: SafetyWing RSVP

Meet and mingle with Ireland’s hottest startups! Enterprise Ireland is BACK at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, and we’re excited to reconnect with old friends and welcome new faces to The Irish Shark Tank at Ireland House for Happy Hour. Availability is limited! Hosted by: Enterprise Ireland RSVP

Korea–US Startup & Investor Networking Night

Join Korean startups, U.S. investors, founders, and technology professionals for an evening of networking and cross-border connection in San Francisco. Organized by KOTRA as part of the Korea Pavilion’s programming, the event brings together Korean startups entering the U.S. market with investors, founders, corporate partners, and members of the Bay Area startup ecosystem.

For those without a ticket to attend TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, KOTRA is offering complimentary Expo+ passes to qualified applicants. Hosted by: KOTRA Silicon Valley RSVP

Vault & Verify: An Evening of Ping Pong, Cocktails & Conversation

Join Skyflow and Descope for an evening of food, cocktails, friendly competition, and conversation with San Francisco’s security, privacy, and identity community. As AI systems become more autonomous, the event brings together leaders working on the challenges of keeping sensitive data and identity secure, with plenty of time to connect away from the conference floor. Hosted by: Descope RSVP

Pursuit of Happiness: Revolutionary Demonstration of Whitney Electrolarynx by Uhura Bionics

Experience a live demonstration of voice-restoration technology as Uhura Bionics co-founder Konrad Zieliński showcases the Whitney Electrolarynx for a U.S. audience. The event explores how technology can help people reclaim their voices and agency following cancer treatment. Hosted by: Uhura Bionics RSVP

Find the 10x Opportunity Hiding in Your Product

Learn how first-principles thinking can uncover overlooked customer needs, strengthen product-market fit, and reveal opportunities for significant growth. The session will use a real-world case study to explore how founders and product teams can identify new opportunities within products they already have. Hosted by: PrincipiumX RSVP

Connect with founders, engineers, and operators building robotics, chips, rockets, and other frontier hardware. This casual, presentation-free gathering offers a chance to swap ideas, share experiences, and meet others working on the challenges of building physical technology. Hosted by: Syntro RSVP

Real World AI: Connect, Invest & Scale in Taiwan

Explore Taiwan’s emerging AI ecosystem through startup pitches and conversations spanning robotics, intelligent hardware, and advanced manufacturing. Meet founders and investors working across Taiwan’s technology landscape and learn more about opportunities to connect, invest, and build. Hosted by: Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs RSVP

Pets of Disrupt: Founders, Investors & Their Pets

Step away from the conference crowd for an informal evening with founders, investors, operators, builders, creators, and the pets that make San Francisco’s startup community a little more human. Hosted by: Omelo RSVP

Connect with founders, revenue leaders, and executives working across go-to-market, partnerships, distribution, and technology. The evening is designed to bring together people building relationships and creating new opportunities across the Bay Area startup ecosystem. Hosted by: EdgeM8 RSVP

Fynex x Orion VC | Curated Rooftop Party

Join founders, operators, and AI-focused investors for a rooftop evening centered on networking, food, drinks, and conversations around AI and infrastructure. Hosted by: Fynex RSVP

Watch It Run: Live Automation Dinner with Bolter

See business automation happen live as Bolter turns attendees’ most dreaded weekly processes into working automations during dinner. Guests can describe a process in plain language and watch as it is transformed into an automation without writing code. Hosted by: Improbable RSVP

The Rooftop Pilaf: An Evening for Tech Founders and Investors

Gather with founders, investors, and growth leaders for a limited-seat rooftop dinner focused on deep tech conversations. The evening pairs a shared meal with an opportunity to connect with others across the technology and investment ecosystem. Hosted by: INNOVA × BeGlobe PR Agency RSVP

SQLDoom Deathmatch Night at Disrupt, hosted by CedarDB

Put your SQL skills to the test in a night of SQLDoom deathmatch, arcade games, food, drinks, and conversation. Play alongside the CedarDB team and connect with database engineers, startup founders, and fellow tech enthusiasts. Hosted by: CedarDB RSVP

Discover emerging Korean startups working across AI, software, medtech, clean tech, digital platforms, and advanced industry. The evening features rapid-fire pitches and networking with founders, investors, and global partners. Hosted by: Brinc RSVP

J-StarX Silicon Valley Extended Program Startup Showcase

Meet 12 Japanese startups building for global markets across AI, enterprise software, health, biotech, defense, agtech, sports tech, and consumer technology. The showcase will feature live demos and opportunities to connect directly with the founders. Hosted by: 500 Global RSVP

Start the day with a casual waterfront run along the Embarcadero, complete with startup-themed “runway” markers. After the run, head to the Ferry Building for coffee and networking with fellow founders and members of the tech community. Hosted by: Handler RSVP

Combine sauna and cold-plunge experiences with conversations and networking around the startups competing in this year’s Startup Battlefield 200. Connect with founders and members of the Startup Battlefield community in a more relaxed setting after Disrupt. Hosted by: Press Club RSVP

Find a Co-founder, Help or Join a Startup

Hear startup pitches before joining breakout groups where attendees can offer feedback, make connections, or explore opportunities to work with the presenting teams. It’s an evening built around meeting founders and finding ways to get involved with early-stage startups. Hosted by: Startup Oasis RSVP

Check the chronological schedule regularly as new Side Events are added weekly.

If you’re building your Disrupt Week calendar, don’t forget the main event.

TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 takes over Moscone West October 13-15, bringing thousands of founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders together under one roof. Come for the programming, stay for the hallway conversations, and leave with a calendar full of people you didn’t know you needed to meet.

Tickets are still available . Come be part of it.

articles.title: a16z-backed EliseAI raises $350M, doubles valuation to $4B
articles.summary: EliseAI raises $350M, doubles valuation in a year.
articles.body:
AI startup EliseAI announced on Tuesday that it has raised $350 million at a $4 billion valuation, double what it was worth when it raised its Series E last August.

This latest round was co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer Ventures. EliseAI, founded in 2017, automates administrative and operational work for housing and healthcare companies. It said its software is used by 1 in 6 apartments across the country and announced this summer it passed $200 million in ARR.

Earlier this month, Elise announced the launch of an AI “teammate” called Apollo that helps with tasks inside the EliseAI platform. “It’s built natively into the same platform that already runs leasing, maintenance, and renewals,” co-founder and CEO Minna Song told TechCrunch. “So it can act across every role on a property team.”

EliseAI also helps automate the patient-related paperwork for specialty physician groups on the healthcare side, “from the first inbound call through referrals, scheduling, insurance verification, chart prep, and follow-up, so nothing falls through the cracks,” she said. The company has targeted housing and healthcare because they are two of the “largest expenses for American households,” she said.

articles.title: Anthropic warns AI may pose ‘existential risks to humanity’ in IPO filing
articles.summary: Anthropic plans to warn potential investors in its initial public offering that advanced artificial intelligence could pose “catastrophic or existential
articles.body: Anthropic plans to warn potential investors in its initial public offering that advanced artificial intelligence could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity,” according to its IPO prospectus reviewed by Reuters.The filing says its AI models could exhibit “self-preserving behaviours,” including attempts to “resist shutdown,” “conceal or manipulate information” and behaviour “resembling blackmail”. “Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm,” Anthropic said.The company, which positions itself as a safety-first AI lab, devoted 80 pages of prospectus’s 261-page main body to risks, nearly twice the 48 pages describing its business. SpaceX, which owns xAI, devoted about 38 of 277 pages to risks.Anthropic said models could develop unexpected capabilities during training that might be discovered only after deployment and had resulted in significant safety incidents. It also warned that models might recognise evaluations and modify their behaviour, limiting safety assessments. Researchers have similarly warned that increasingly capable models can recognise when they are being watched and adjust their behaviour, complicating monitoring.Anthropic and other developers, including OpenAI, have faced scrutiny after experimental systems defied constraints, including a reported breach of Australia’s health-system database by an OpenAI model. Anthropic safety researcher Evan Hubinger estimated a greater than 10% probability that AI could kill humans within the next decade, echoing former colleague Jacob Coxon.Despite emphasising safety, Anthropic said returns on such investment were unclear and did not disclose its spending. Earlier this month, it said safety work used about 6% of its AI research computing power during a sample week in July. It called safety efforts “resource-intensive” and said limited funds must be divided among computing power, costly AI talent and safety.The Claude developer said customer usage and revenue depended on new models and that a “continuous and overlapping cadence” of releases was “inherent to remaining at the frontier of AI development.” Last week, it released a new Opus model, 10 days after CEO Dario Amodei published a nearly 4,000-word essay urging the frontier to be paced.Anthropic has pledged to publish more data on its use of AI models to build future generations as experts warn about recursive self-improvement, when models develop without human help. Anthropic declined to comment. Analysts said slowing down could hand rivals an advantage. Anthropic declined to comment in response to a request for comment.You use AI every day.
